thesis: The strongest short thesis is structural AI commoditization. Generative models can collapse the value of standalone creative tools, reduce switching costs, and shift monetization toward model providers or new agentic interfaces. Adobe's 13% revenue growth and >150% AI-first ARR are encouraging, but could still represent defensive bundling rather than incremental economic rent. The balance sheet and cash flow, however, make this a moat-duration risk rather than a survival risk.

evidence.claim: Q3 revenue grew 13% y/y while AI-first ARR grew >150% y/y.
Current market price is far below the locked Base DCF, implying the market is pricing significant structural risk.
Adobe still spends heavily on R&D and AI while defending multiple product categories.

counterevidence: >1B MAU and large RPO indicate continued workflow relevance.
Aggressive buybacks convert cash generation into per-share value.
falsifiers: Sustained AI-driven ARR acceleration weakens the short thesis; declining ARR despite rising AI usage strengthens it.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 경영진 정직성 또는 회계 신뢰성 훼손

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Large recurring OCF funds operations and capital allocation.
Share count is shrinking through repurchases.
Subscription ARR and usage support real customer value.
Risk exists, but current ARR/usage does not establish persistent shrinkage.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 현재가격이 비현실적인 Bull Case 이상을 요구
단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Revenue is diversified across creative, documents and enterprise experience.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Recurring cash flow and moderate leverage make this unlikely.
